name: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework (2nd edition)
publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission, Singapore
licenseNote: The Model AI Governance Framework is published by Singapore's IMDA and PDPC. AEGIS summarises its four areas in original wording under its own identifiers and does not reproduce the framework's text. Mapping an AEGIS record to an entry here is not a conformance statement.
description: The four areas of Singapore's voluntary model framework for responsible AI deployment: internal governance, the level of human involvement in AI-augmented decisions, operations management, and stakeholder interaction, with the AEGIS records that evidence each.

controls.title: Clear roles and responsibilities for AI
controls.summary: Accountability for the ethical deployment of AI sits with named people and bodies, with oversight from senior management.

controls.title: Risk management and internal controls
controls.summary: Risks from AI use are identified and managed through internal controls, including policies on data, models and the actions AI may take.

controls.title: Staff training and awareness
controls.summary: People who develop, deploy or oversee AI understand the governance framework and their part in it.

controls.title: Severity and probability of harm
controls.summary: The level of human involvement in each AI-augmented decision is chosen from the probability and severity of harm to people.
controls.category: Determining the level of human involvement

controls.title: Human in, over or out of the loop
controls.summary: Decisions are classified as human-in-the-loop, human-over-the-loop or human-out-of-the-loop, and the choice is recorded and reviewed.
controls.category: Determining the level of human involvement

controls.title: Data quality and lineage
controls.summary: Data used by AI models is understood, of adequate quality, with its lineage and any bias examined and recorded.

controls.title: Model explainability, repeatability and robustness
controls.summary: Models and the decisions they influence can be explained, repeated with the same inputs, and withstand errors and adversarial inputs.

controls.title: Monitoring, auditability and review
controls.summary: AI systems are monitored in operation, their decisions are auditable, and models and controls are reviewed and tuned over time.

controls.title: Communication with users and the public
controls.summary: People are told when AI is used, what it does and how it affects them, in language they can understand.

controls.title: Feedback and recourse
controls.summary: Affected people can ask questions, give feedback and seek review of AI-influenced decisions, and those channels are acted on.
